# Bands and direction rules

## Augmentation vs automation share (Anthropic Economic Index) (`aei_augmentation_share`)

- Band input: `anthropic_ei.global.augmentation_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal 0.5 to inf; fast -inf to 0.4; falsifying none. Normal = augmentation at least half of classified use; fast = automation clearly dominant (augmentation under 40%). Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: the report classifies conversations from its sampling week, published within weeks.

## Occupations with a quarter of their tasks using Claude (`aei_occupation_depth_25`)

- Band input: `anthropic_ei.global.occupations_25pct_tasks_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.6; fast 0.8 to inf; falsifying none. The share only rises, so the question is how fast. Normal = under 60% of occupations with a quarter of their tasks in use four years in; fast = 80% or more. Anchor: 49% in the March 2026 report (data 5-12 February 2026).
- Timing: Coincident: it classifies usage from the report's sampling week, published in that report.

## ARC-AGI-2 best score (`arc_agi_frontier`)

- Band input: `metric:arc_agi_frontier` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.5; fast 0.85 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under half (the 2025 frontier); fast = 85% or above (the ARC Prize grand-prize bar). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: benchmark gains on novel reasoning come before products can rely on that reasoning.

## US adults who have used generative AI (`bbd_adult_use`)

- Band input: `fred.us_adults.any_use_share.q` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.75; fast 0.9 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = up to three quarters of adults four years after launch (the internet took about a decade to reach that share of US adults); fast = near-universal use at the same age. Anchors: 44.6% in the first FRED wave (Q3 2024) and 61.8% in Q2 2026.
- Timing: Coincident: the survey records use up to the interview, published within a quarter via FRED.

## Share of work hours assisted by generative AI (`bbd_work_hours_assisted`)

- Band input: `fred.us_workers.hours_assisted_share.q` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.09; fast 0.2 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = single-digit share of hours in year three (PCs and the internet were here at the same age); fast = more than 20% of hours assisted.
- Timing: Coincident: the survey records hours assisted in the week before the interview, published within a quarter.

## US workers using generative AI for work every day (`bbd_work_use_daily`)

- Band input: `fed_board.us_workers.genai_work_use_daily_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.15; fast 0.3 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = up to about one worker in seven using generative AI every working day, the pace of an office tool diffusing over years; fast = three in ten or more, daily use at the level of email. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Coincident: daily work use moves with adoption itself, measured in the same wave.

## US labour productivity, year on year (`bls_labor_productivity_yoy`)

- Band input: `bls.prs85006091.q` (pct)
- Rule: normal -inf to 2.5; fast 3.5 to inf; falsifying none. Post-war nonfarm productivity growth averages about 2.1% a year, so anything up to 2.5% is trend. Goldman's AI scenario adds about 1.5 points a year; sustained prints of 3.5% or more would be that. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: output per hour rises only after firms reorganise work around a tool, and BLS prints it a quarter late and revises it.

## US total factor productivity, private nonfarm business (`bls_tfp_private_nonfarm`)

- Band input: `metric:bls_tfp_yoy` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.012; fast 0.02 to inf; falsifying none. Long-run private nonfarm TFP growth is about 1% a year; Acemoglu's AI estimate is at most 0.66% over a decade, invisible at annual resolution. Goldman-scale is roughly a point a year on top of trend. Normal = at most 1.2%; fast = 2% or more.
- Timing: Lagging: total factor productivity is annual, published months after the year ends, and moves only after complementary investment pays off.

## US firms using AI (Census BTOS) (`btos_firm_use`)

- Band input: `census_btos.us.ai_use_share_v2.2w` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.35; fast 0.5 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under about a third of firms in year three, the pace at which PCs and e-commerce reached half of firms over a decade or more; fast = more than half. Ramp's card-spend index (>50%) is a different instrument and not comparable.
- Timing: Coincident: firms report use in the last two weeks, and Census publishes every two weeks.

## California unemployment claims from AI-exposed occupations (`cait_high_exposure_claims`)

- Band input: `metric:cait_high_exposure_claims_3mma_mom` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.02; fast 0.05 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = monthly moves of up to 2% in the smoothed series, the noise floor of claims data; fast = 5% or more month on month, sustained. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: new unemployment claims rise before employment and wage statistics reflect job losses.

## Customer-support productivity uplift from a generative-AI assistant (`call_center_uplift`)

- Band input: `nber.customer_support_agents.productivity_uplift.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.2; fast 0.5 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = an average uplift under 20%, the range prior process tools (CRM, knowledge bases) delivered in the same job; fast = 50% or more, the order of magnitude the fast scenario needs from a single tool. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: the field experiment measured resolution rates while agents used the assistant.

## Entry-level employment shortfall in AI-exposed occupations (`canaries_entry_level_gap`)

- Band input: `stanford_del.us_entry_level_exposed.employment_gap.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.1; fast 0.25 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = a shortfall under 10 points, inside the range youth employment swings over a cycle; fast = 25 points or more. The current reading sits between, so it is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: firms stop hiring juniors before they cut existing staff, so entry-level gaps open first.

## Employment in AI-exposed occupations, year on year (`canaries_exposed_employment_yoy`)

- Band input: `canaries.us_exposure_q5.employment_yoy.m` (share)
- Rule: normal -0.01 to 0.01; fast -inf to -0.03; falsifying none. Normal = within one percent of flat, ordinary occupational churn; fast = a 3% or worse decline in exposed occupations, which is what a broad AI-attributable displacement looks like in payroll data. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: monthly payroll records employment as it changes, published with a few weeks' lag.

## Hyperscaler capex to AI revenue (trailing year) (`capex_to_revenue_stack`)

- Band input: `metric:capex_to_revenue_stack` (ratio)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.3, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; a move under 0.3x is run-rate noise. Rising = capex pulling further ahead of revenue (the bet growing); falling = revenue catching the buildout.
- Timing: Leading: capex is committed years before the capacity earns, so the ratio signals over- or under-building ahead of returns.

## Circular financing scale (`circular_financing_scale`)

- Band input: `metric:circular_commitments_new_4q` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 3 periods, dead band 20000000000.0, higher is concentrating. Three quarters of the trailing-year flow; moves under $20B are one small deal. Rising commitments concentrate the stack's financing on a few counterparties, and unlike the cumulative total this series can fall.
- Timing: Leading: vendor financing is signed before the compute is delivered or used, so commitments run ahead of revenue and capacity.

## Vendors claiming shipped continual learning (`cl_lab_release_claims`)

- Band input: `metric:cl_lab_release_claims_12m` (count)
- Rule: normal -inf to 3.0; fast 6.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = up to three builders a year claiming shipped continual learning; fast = six or more, including a frontier-lab release branded continual or online learning (the ladder's L5 made observable). Every row is tier 7, so the status caps at emerging.
- Timing: Leading: vendors ship learning systems before labour or productivity series could register what they do.

## Fastest production refresh of a continually updated model (hours) (`cl_refresh_cadence_hours`)

- Band input: `metric:cl_refresh_cadence_hours` (hours)
- Rule: normal 1.0 to inf; fast -inf to 0.25; falsifying none. Normal = an hour or more between learning from use and serving the update, the pace of a retrain-and-redeploy pipeline; fast = a quarter of an hour or less, updates flowing near-continuously. Every row is a vendor describing itself (tier 7), so the status caps at emerging.
- Timing: Leading: the refresh interval shortens before continual learning shows in products or capability.

## Concentration among covered cloud filers (HHI) (`cloud_hhi`)

- Band input: `metric:hhi_by_layer` (index)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four calendar quarters; a move under 200 HHI points is noise.
- Timing: Leading: buyers shift workloads between clouds before pricing is renegotiated, so share moves ahead of margins.

## Cloud backlog (remaining performance obligations) (`cloud_rpo_backlog`)

- Band input: `sec.orcl.rpo.q` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 10000000000.0, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; moves under $10B are noise at this scale. Growing backlog concentrates future cloud revenue in a few contracts.
- Timing: Leading: backlog is contracted revenue not yet recognised, so it moves quarters before cloud revenue and the margins that follow.

## Cloud segment operating margins (`cloud_segment_margins`)

- Band input: `metric:segment_operating_margin` (share)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four fiscal quarters; two points of margin is noise. Rising cloud margin under rising capex means the layer is keeping surplus.
- Timing: Lagging: cloud margins absorb depreciation on capex spent years earlier and are filed a quarter after the fact.

## Consumer surplus from generative AI (willingness to accept) (`consumer_surplus_wta`)

- Band input: `stanford_del.us.genai_consumer_surplus_usd.pt` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 1 periods, dead band 10000000000.0, higher is dispersing. Two annual waves so far, so the trend is one step; moves under $10B are within survey error. Rising surplus disperses value away from producers to consumers.
- Timing: Lagging: surplus estimates come from surveys of habits users have already formed and publish months after fieldwork.

## Continual-learning ladder (highest production rung) (`continual_learning_level`)

- Band input: `metric:continual_learning_level` (rung)
- Rule: normal -inf to 3.0; fast 5.0 to inf; falsifying none. Appendix E's rule: L0-L3 (memory, population-level online learning, per-customer adapters) is normal; L5-L6 (persistent per-session weight updates, the six-month-employee test) is fast; L4 (organisation knowledge in weights) is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: learning on the job would feed deployment back into capability before labour or productivity series could show it.

## Cross-tracker concordance (labour) (`cross_tracker_concordance`)

- Band input: `metric:cross_tracker_concordance` (count)
- Rule: normal -inf to 1.0; fast 2.0 to inf; falsifying 3.0 to inf. Normal = at most one tracker past its threshold; fast = two; falsifying = three or more concurrently, per the thesis rules in the brief.
- Timing: Coincident: it counts how many monthly labour trackers read past their thresholds at the latest release.

## Non-Nvidia share of AI compute shipped (H100-equivalents) (`custom_silicon_share`)

- Band input: `metric:custom_silicon_share` (share)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is dispersing. Four quarters; under two points is inside Epoch's estimate ranges. Rising non-Nvidia share = the chip layer's rent dispersing.
- Timing: Leading: chips shipped now set the compute mix that serves models over the next several years.

## Hyperscaler server useful lives (10-K estimates) (`depreciation_useful_life_changes`)

- Band input: `sec_filing.amzn.server_useful_life_years.fy` (years)
- Rule: direction over 2 periods, dead band 0.4, higher is dispersing. Two annual readings; a change under half a year is rounding. A shorter life means faster hardware turnover and thinner margins for the layer, so shortening reads as dispersing.
- Timing: Lagging: useful-life estimates change in annual 10-Ks after the hardware has served long enough to judge.

## Developer productivity uplift (METR RCTs) (`dev_rct_uplift`)

- Band input: `metr_blog.rct_2026.dev_speed_change.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.2; fast 0.4 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = uplift of at most about 20%, setting-dependent (the range of controlled studies to date); fast = broad uplift above 40%, the scale the productivity-boom claims need.
- Timing: Leading: controlled trials show what tools do to working speed before firms reorganise work around them.

## Enterprise multi-model usage share (Menlo) (`enterprise_multi_homing_share`)

- Band input: `menlo.enterprise.multi_model_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: direction over 2 periods, dead band 0.05, higher is dispersing. Annual waves; a move under five points is survey noise. More multi-homing disperses the model layer's pricing power.
- Timing: Coincident: the survey records how many models firms use now, published with each annual wave.

## Enterprise pilots with measurable P&L impact (`enterprise_pilot_to_production`)

- Band input: `nanda.us_enterprise.pilots_with_pnl_impact_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.1; fast 0.3 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = at most 10% of pilots with measurable P&L impact, the typical enterprise-IT hit rate; fast = more than 30%.
- Timing: Coincident: the survey records whether this year's pilots are paying off now.

## Application layer's share of enterprise generative-AI spend (Menlo) (`enterprise_spend_by_layer`)

- Band input: `metric:enterprise_app_spend_share` (share)
- Rule: direction over 1 periods, dead band 0.05, higher is concentrating. Two annual waves, so the trend is one step; a move under five points is within survey error. Rising application share = value concentrating at the application layer.
- Timing: Coincident: the survey records budgets enterprises are spending this year, published once a year.

## Public text data exhaustion year (Epoch projection) (`epoch_data_exhaustion_year`)

- Band input: `epoch_blog.public_text.exhaustion_year.pt` (year)
- Rule: normal 2028.0 to inf; fast -inf to 2026.0; falsifying none. Normal = exhaustion in 2028 or later (the paper's compute-optimal case); fast = 2026 or earlier (the overtrained case, which is what the AI 2027 scenario's compute path implies). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: the projected exhaustion year constrains training plans years before it binds.

## Inference price at fixed capability (halving time) (`epoch_inference_price_fixed_capability`)

- Band input: `metric:inference_price_halving_days` (days)
- Rule: normal 230.0 to inf; fast -inf to 110.0; falsifying none. Normal = halving no faster than every 230 days (about 3x a year, the hardware pace); fast = every 110 days or less (10x a year or more; Epoch's reading at this threshold is faster still). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Coincident: prices fall the day a cheaper model matches the benchmark, when buyers can switch.

## Frontier training compute growth (doubling time) (`epoch_training_compute_growth`)

- Band input: `metric:training_compute_doubling_days` (days)
- Rule: normal 300.0 to inf; fast -inf to 182.0; falsifying none. Normal = doubling no faster than every 300 days (about 2.3x a year, the pre-2010 pace of compute growth); fast = every 182 days or less (4x a year or more, Epoch's 2010-2025 trend). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: training compute sets the capability of models released months later and deployed years later.

## Training power draw growth (doubling time) (`epoch_training_power_growth`)

- Band input: `metric:training_power_doubling_days` (days)
- Rule: normal 365.0 to inf; fast -inf to 230.0; falsifying none. Normal = doubling no faster than yearly (grid-connection pace); fast = every 230 days or less (3x a year, the pace a runaway buildout needs). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: power drawn for training reflects data-centre capacity built earlier and caps the models released next.

## Executives reporting no AI impact on their own firm (`exec_reported_impact`)

- Band input: `nber.executives_4_countries.no_ai_impact_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal 0.7 to inf; fast -inf to 0.4; falsifying none. Normal = at least 70% of firms report no measurable impact three years in, as with PCs at the same age; fast = a majority reporting impact (no-impact share under 40%). Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: executives report impact on their firm only after it shows in results, surveyed and published with a lag.

## Expert-data market run-rate (Mercor) (`expert_data_market_run_rate`)

- Band input: `dealroom.mercor.gross_revenue_run_rate_usd.pt` (USD)
- Rule: normal -inf to 1000000000.0; fast 2000000000.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = the largest vendor under one billion gross, the scale the data-labelling leaders reached over a decade; fast = two billion or more at a single vendor, doubling within a year. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: labs buy expert data for models they will release months later.

## Workers highly exposed to AI with low adaptive capacity (`exposed_low_adaptive_workers`)

- Band input: `nber.us_workers.high_exposure_low_adaptive_capacity.pt` (workers)
- Rule: normal -inf to 5000000.0; fast 10000000.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under five million workers (about 3% of the workforce), the scale of the China trade shock spread over a decade; fast = ten million or more. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: it counts workers likely to struggle before displacement happens, from exposure and adaptive capacity measured now.

## Usage as a share of theoretical exposure (`exposure_vs_usage_gap`)

- Band input: `metric:exposure_vs_usage_gap` (ratio)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.6; fast 0.8 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under 60% of exposed workers use the tools weekly three years in; fast = 80% or more, the gap closed. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: current weekly use is divided by a fixed exposure estimate, so it moves with use.

## FDA-authorised AI-enabled devices, growth (`fda_ai_devices_cumulative`)

- Band input: `metric:fda_ai_devices_yoy` (pct_change_yoy)
- Rule: normal -inf to 50.0; fast 100.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = the cumulative count growing under 50% a year (the 2019-2024 pace); fast = doubling or faster, which is what an ungated regulated domain would show. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Coincident: authorisations arrive as devices reach market, published as the FDA updates its list.

## FDA-authorised devices built on a large language model (`fda_first_llm_device`)

- Band input: `metric:fda_llm_devices_count` (count)
- Rule: normal -inf to 3.0; fast 10.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = a handful of LLM-based authorisations by end-2026, given a 510(k) path of roughly six months and a first clearance in December 2025; fast = ten or more, the regulatory throughput a fast scenario needs. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: the first language-model devices clear review before clinical use spreads.

## Frontier labs' share of tracked venture dollars (`frontier_capital_concentration`)

- Band input: `metric:frontier_share_of_venture_dollars` (share)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.05, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; a move under five points is a single round's timing. Rising = capital concentrating in the frontier labs.
- Timing: Leading: venture rounds fund capacity and hiring that produce revenue a year or more later.

## Frontier models completing expert legal tasks end to end (Harvey LAB) (`harvey_lab_frontier_completion`)

- Band input: `harvey_blog.lab_holdout.all_pass_top_model.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.3; fast 0.7 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = the best frontier model completes under 30% of expert tasks end to end; fast = above 70%, where substitution rather than assistance becomes the product. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: end-to-end completion on a legal benchmark comes before firms trust agents with the same work.

## 50%/80% horizon ratio (`horizon_ratio_80_50`)

- Band input: `metric:horizon_ratio_80_50` (ratio)
- Rule: normal 5.0 to inf; fast -inf to 2.0; falsifying none. Normal = ratio ≥ 5 (gap holding or widening); fast = ratio ≤ 2. The falsifying condition (≤ 2 AND 80% horizon > 8 h) is compound and lives in the thesis monitor, not the band.
- Timing: Leading: the gap between occasional and reliable success closes before agents can be deployed unsupervised.

## Chatbot effect on earnings and hours in exposed occupations (Denmark) (`humlum_precise_null`)

- Band input: `humlum_pdf.denmark_exposed_workers.chatbot_effect_on_earnings.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -0.02 to 0.02; fast -inf to -0.05; falsifying none. Normal = earnings and hours effects within two percent two years in; fast = a decline of five percent or more for exposed workers. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: administrative earnings records show effects years after adoption, published after linkage and review.

## Internal-to-public deployment gap at the frontier (`internal_external_deployment_gap_months`)

- Band input: `dwarkesh.anthropic_mythos.internal_to_public_gap_months.pt` (months)
- Rule: normal -inf to 6.0; fast 12.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = a gap under six months, ordinary red-teaming and productisation; fast = a year or more, a lab running internally on a model the public does not have. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: capabilities exist inside labs before the public can use them, by the months this measures.

## Lab concentration of routed tokens (OpenRouter, HHI) (`lab_hhi`)

- Band input: `metric:lab_token_hhi` (index)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four weekly readings; under 0.02 in the index is table churn. Rising = routed tokens concentrating on fewer labs.
- Timing: Leading: developers move routed traffic between labs within days of a release, ahead of enterprise contracts and revenue.

## Labs buying from the training-input layer (enter bell) (`lab_procurement_signal`)

- Band input: `metric:lab_procurement_signal_4q` (score)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 1.0, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; a one-point move is one vendor's single disclosure. Rising = the labs buying more from the training-input layer.
- Timing: Leading: labs buy data and environments for models released months later, so purchases precede capability and revenue.

## Lab recoupment ratio (`lab_recoupment_ratio`)

- Band input: `metric:lab_recoupment_ratio` (ratio)
- Rule: direction over 3 periods, dead band 0.05, higher is concentrating. Three points; a move under 0.05 is noise. A rising ratio means the lab is recouping capital faster than it raises it.
- Timing: Lagging: revenue earned against capital already raised accumulates slowly, after the funding and pricing decisions behind it.

## Frontier-lab revenue run-rates (`lab_run_rates`)

- Band input: `epoch.openai.revenue_run_rate_usd.pt` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 2000000000.0, higher is concentrating. Four reports; moves under $2B are reporting noise. Rising run-rate concentrates revenue at the two frontier labs.

## Frontier lab valuation to run-rate multiple (`lab_valuation_to_run_rate`)

- Band input: `metric:post_money_to_arr_multiple` (ratio)
- Rule: direction over 3 periods, dead band 3.0, higher is concentrating. Three valuation events; a move under 3x is noise in press-reported run-rates. Rising = the market pricing more durable rents into the labs.

## Lab vertical integration (acquisitions and acquihires, trailing four quarters) (`lab_vertical_integration_exit_bell`)

- Band input: `metric:lab_vertical_integration_events_4q` (count)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 1.0, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; one event is not a trend. More deals per year concentrate the application layer into the labs.
- Timing: Leading: an acquisition is announced before the acquired layer's economics change, so the count moves ahead of margins.

## US labour share of income, year on year (`labor_share_nonfarm`)

- Band input: `metric:bls_labor_share_yoy` (share)
- Rule: normal -0.02 to inf; fast -inf to -0.05; falsifying none. Normal = year-on-year moves of at most 2%, the size of ordinary cyclical swings in the index; fast = 5% or worse a year, roughly the pace that takes the share from 60% to 45% by 2030 (the extreme scenario). Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: the labour share moves only as wages and profits adjust to productivity, and BLS revises it for years.

## Semiconductors' share of stack operating income (`margin_stack_semis_share`)

- Band input: `metric:margin_stack_share_by_layer` (share)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four calendar quarters; a move under two points is within fiscal-calendar noise. Rising semis share = rent concentrating at the chip layer; falling = migrating up.
- Timing: Lagging: segment operating income is filed a quarter after it is earned and reflects contracts signed well before.

## METR 50% time horizon (`metr_horizon_50`)

- Band input: `metric:horizon_doubling_days_50_since_2024` (minutes)
- Rule: normal 213.0 to inf; fast -inf to 122.0; falsifying none. Normal = doubling time ≥ 7 months (≈213 days, METR's 2019–2025 trend); fast = ≤ 4 months (≈122 days), the AI 2027 assumption. Between the two is `emerging`. The bands are about the current pace, so the input is a log-linear fit over the 2024-onward window, the most recent window METR reports (89 days in the TH1.1 post of 29 Jan 2026), recomputed from METR's corrected data. On the 2023-onward window METR's published figure is 128.7 days, in the gap between the bands: the reading is window-sensitive and both numbers are shown.
- Timing: Leading: benchmark capability moves months before products are built on it and years before adoption or productivity series register it.

## METR 80% time horizon (`metr_horizon_80`)

- Band input: `metric:horizon_doubling_days_80_since_2024` (minutes)
- Rule: normal 213.0 to inf; fast -inf to 122.0; falsifying none. Same bands and same 2024-onward window as the 50% horizon, applied to our own fit because METR publishes doubling times for the 50% series only. The 2023-onward fit (horizon_doubling_days_80) sits in the gap between the bands.
- Timing: Leading: reliable task length is what products need, and it moves before the products that depend on it ship.

## Price per unit of capability (cheapest METR-hour on OpenRouter) (`model_price_per_horizon_hour`)

- Band input: `metric:frontier_price_per_horizon_hour` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four price change-points; a move under two cents per million tokens per horizon-hour is noise. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.
- Timing: Coincident: list prices change the day a lab reprices or releases, the moment capability becomes purchasable.

## Price per unit of capability (cheapest near-frontier model, Artificial Analysis) (`model_price_per_intelligence_point`)

- Band input: `metric:aa_frontier_price_per_point` (USD)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.0006, higher is concentrating. Four price change-points; a move under $0.0006 per million tokens per index point (about a tenth of the 11 Sep 2026 level) is one model's repricing. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.
- Timing: Coincident: a model's price and index arrive together at release, so the ratio moves when the market does.

## Model-layer token concentration on OpenRouter (HHI, top table) (`model_token_concentration`)

- Band input: `metric:model_token_hhi_top10` (index)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Weekly readings; moves under 0.02 in the index are table churn. A rising index means routed tokens concentrating on fewer models.

## Neocloud borrowing cost (CoreWeave facility rates) (`neocloud_debt_terms`)

- Band input: `metric:neocloud_weighted_facility_rate` (share)
- Rule: direction over 3 periods, dead band 0.01, higher is concentrating. Three quarter-ends; moves under a percentage point are facility mix. Rising rates concentrate the compute layer's returns with its lenders.
- Timing: Coincident: facility rates are priced on current lender appetite and reported at each quarter end.

## Recent-graduate unemployment rate (NY Fed) (`new_grad_unemployment`)

- Band input: `nyfed.us_recent_grads.unemployment_rate.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.06; fast 0.08 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = up to 6%, the top of the 2010s range for recent graduates; fast = 8% or more outside a recession. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: graduates meet the labour market after hiring plans are set, and the series is a smoothed average.

## Open-weights gap to the closed frontier (ECI points) (`open_vs_closed_gap`)

- Band input: `metric:open_vs_closed_gap` (index)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 2.0, higher is concentrating. Four open-weights releases; a move under two ECI points is inside the index's confidence intervals. Widening gap = rents concentrating in the closed labs.
- Timing: Leading: open-weights releases close the capability gap before prices and shares in the model layer respond.

## Open-weights lag behind the closed frontier (months) (`open_weights_lag_months`)

- Band input: `metric:open_weights_lag_months` (months)
- Rule: normal 9.0 to inf; fast -inf to 3.0; falsifying none. Normal = open weights at least nine months behind, roughly a model generation; fast = three months or less, when a closed lead lasts about one release cycle. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: an open model that matches the frontier arrives before prices and market shares in the model layer adjust to it.

## Work-related share of ChatGPT consumer messages (`openai_work_share`)

- Band input: `openai_blog.chatgpt_consumer.work_related_message_share.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.4; fast 0.6 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under 40% of consumer messages are work-related, as personal use led with PCs and the web; fast = a work majority, meaning the consumer product has been pulled into production workflows. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: the share describes what users did in the sampled period, published months later.

## Ord half-life misfit (observed 50/80 ratio vs constant hazard) (`ord_half_life_misfit`)

- Band input: `metric:ord_half_life_misfit` (ratio)
- Rule: normal 1.5 to inf; fast -inf to 1.1; falsifying none. Normal = misfit of 1.5 or more (observed ratios of 5-10x against the constant-hazard 3.1x, the pattern since 2024); fast = within 10% of the constant-hazard prediction, which would mean long-task reliability tracking short-task success. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: a change in how reliability scales with task length would show in benchmarks before deployment changes.

## Agent reliability across repeated runs (tau-bench pass^k) (`pass_hat_k_tau_bench`)

- Band input: `automation_anywhere.tau_bench_leaderboard_1.pass_hat_4.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.7; fast 0.9 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under 70% of tasks pass all four runs, so the best agent still fails one attempt in three; fast = 90% or more at k of four or higher, the reliability a workflow can be built on. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: reliability across repeated runs is what deployment needs, and it moves in benchmarks before agents ship widely.

## Hardware price-performance growth (doubling time) (`perf_per_dollar_growth`)

- Band input: `metric:perf_per_dollar_doubling_days` (days)
- Rule: normal 500.0 to inf; fast -inf to 365.0; falsifying none. Normal = doubling no faster than every 500 days (roughly the +49% a year Epoch reports); fast = yearly or faster. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: cheaper compute per dollar lowers the cost of the models and inference that arrive over the following years.

## Wage premium for AI skills (PwC AI Jobs Barometer) (`pwc_ai_skill_wage_premium`)

- Band input: `pwc.ai_skilled_workers.wage_premium.fy` (share)
- Rule: normal 0.25 to 0.75; fast 1.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = a premium between 25% and 75%, large but of the size prior scarce IT skills carried; fast = a premium of 100% or more, wages doubling for a skill. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: job ads state the wage employers offer for the skill now.

## US businesses paying for AI (Ramp AI Index) (`ramp_paid_ai_adoption`)

- Band input: `ramp.us_businesses.paid_ai_adoption_share.m` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.45; fast 0.65 to inf; falsifying none. Ramp's customers are younger and more tech-forward than the Census universe (56% here against 22% in BTOS at the same date), so the BTOS edges (a third, a half) do not transfer. Normal = under 45% of Ramp customers paying in year four; fast = 65% or more, i.e. most of even this sample paying. Between is emerging. The trend carries more information than the level: +0.4 points in August 2026 after a year of roughly a point a month.
- Timing: Leading: paid subscriptions come before measurable use at scale, and card data arrives within weeks.

## Exposed vs unexposed occupation employment gap (Revelio) (`revelio_exposed_vs_unexposed_growth`)

- Band input: `revelio.us_exposed.growth_gap.m` (share)
- Rule: normal -0.05 to inf; fast -inf to -0.1; falsifying none. Normal = a relative gap of at most 5 points over nearly four years, within the drift between occupation groups in any period; fast = a 10-point or larger gap. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: online profiles track employment month by month, published within weeks.

## Active RL-environment vendors (directory count) (`rl_environment_vendor_count`)

- Band input: `rl_list.commercial.active_vendor_count.pt` (count)
- Rule: normal -inf to 60.0; fast 150.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = a few dozen vendors (a specialist market); fast = 150 or more (a commodity market forming in months). Between is emerging.
- Timing: Leading: vendors sell training environments for models that ship months later.

## Agent-workdays per human workday in frontier research (self-reported) (`rsi_agent_workdays_per_human`)

- Band input: `openai_blog.openai.rsi_agent_workdays_per_human.pt` (ratio)
- Rule: normal -inf to 1.0; fast 3.0 to inf; falsifying none. Below one agent-day per human-day, agents are tools inside a human-run process (normal); at three or more, most research effort is agent effort, the regime the AI 2027 'R&D multiplier' assumes (fast). Between is emerging. Tier 7 evidence caps the status at emerging whatever the number says.
- Timing: Leading: agent effort inside research labs runs ahead of the capability it produces by a model generation or more.

## Human interventions on 4–8 hour agent tasks (self-reported) (`rsi_intervention_rate_4_8h`)

- Band input: `openai_blog.openai.rsi_intervention_rate_4_8h.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal 0.5 to inf; fast -inf to 0.25; falsifying none. Humans steering most long tasks (half or more need intervention) is the normal-technology picture; a quarter or fewer is the regime where long agent runs are autonomous. Between is emerging. The reported value is a floor ('over half'), stored as 0.5.
- Timing: Leading: fewer interventions on long internal tasks come before agents are trusted with the same work outside the lab.

## Safety brakes inside the labs (events, trailing year) (`safety_brake_events`)

- Band input: `metric:safety_brake_events_12m` (count)
- Rule: normal 1.0 to inf; fast -inf to 0.0; falsifying none. Normal = at least one announced brake a year (the limits bind); fast = none, the pace the AI 2027 scenario assumes on the invention stage. Lab self-reports are tier 7, so the status is capped at emerging until an independent record exists.
- Timing: Leading: a lab pauses or gates before a release reaches users, so brakes show before any deployment slows.

## Concentration among covered chip filers (HHI) (`semis_hhi`)

- Band input: `metric:hhi_by_layer` (index)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.02, higher is concentrating. Four calendar quarters; a move under 200 HHI points is noise. Rising = the covered chip layer concentrating further.
- Timing: Leading: a challenger's revenue share moves before the incumbent's pricing power erodes, so concentration falls ahead of margins.

## Rent concentration in semiconductors (`semis_rent_concentration`)

- Band input: `metric:gross_margin` (share)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.01, higher is concentrating. Four fiscal quarters; a move under one point of margin is noise. Rising margin = rent concentrating at the chip layer.
- Timing: Lagging: chip margins reflect orders placed quarters earlier and are filed a quarter after they are earned.

## Startups' share of enterprise AI application revenue (`startup_share_of_app_revenue`)

- Band input: `menlo.us_enterprise.startup_app_revenue_share.fy` (share)
- Rule: direction over 1 periods, dead band 0.05, higher is dispersing. Two annual waves, so the trend is one step; under five points is survey error. Rising startup share = value dispersing away from incumbents.
- Timing: Coincident: the annual survey records where this year's application spend goes.

## US state AI bills introduced (legislative year) (`state_ai_bills_introduced`)

- Band input: `ncsl.us.ai_bills_introduced.a` (count)
- Rule: normal 500.0 to inf; fast -inf to 200.0; falsifying none. Normal = five hundred or more bills a year (the 2024-2025 volume, legislatures reacting at their own speed); fast = under two hundred, legislatures standing aside. Between is emerging.
- Timing: Lagging: bills follow public attention to deployments already under way, and counts settle after the legislative year.

## Progress against the AI 2027 quantitative predictions (`surprise_index`)

- Band input: `metric:surprise_index` (share)
- Rule: normal -inf to 0.6; fast 0.9 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = 60% or less of the predicted pace (a delay that compounds to years); fast = 90% or more (on schedule). Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: grading predictions against capability benchmarks shows the pace before labour or productivity series can.

## Freelance writing earnings after ChatGPT (Upwork) (`upwork_freelancer_effects`)

- Band input: `cepr_voxeu.upwork_writing_freelancers.monthly_earnings_change.pt` (share)
- Rule: normal -0.1 to 0.0; fast -inf to -0.2; falsifying none. Normal = declines under 10% in the most substitutable freelance categories, a tool effect at the margin; fast = a 20% or worse collapse in freelance earnings. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Leading: freelance marketplaces reprice exposed work within months, ahead of employment inside firms.

## Vertical versus horizontal application funding (`vertical_vs_horizontal_apps`)

- Band input: `metric:vertical_vs_horizontal_apps` (ratio)
- Rule: direction over 4 periods, dead band 0.2, higher is concentrating. Four quarters; a move under 0.2x is round timing. Rising = capital concentrating in vertical applications.
- Timing: Leading: funding follows investors' expectations of which applications will earn, a year or more before revenue shows it.

## Waymo paid rides per week (`waymo_weekly_paid_rides`)

- Band input: `techcrunch.waymo.weekly_paid_rides.pt` (rides_per_week)
- Rule: normal -inf to 1000000.0; fast 5000000.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = under a million paid rides a week, well under one percent of US ride-hail trips and scaling one city at a time; fast = five million or more, a national-scale substitution. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Coincident: rides are counted as they happen and stated by the company in periodic updates.

## Occupational-mix dissimilarity since ChatGPT (Yale Budget Lab) (`yale_occupational_mix_dissimilarity`)

- Band input: `yale_budget_lab_data.us_workers.occupation_dissimilarity_pp.m` (pp)
- Rule: normal -inf to 7.5; fast 10.0 to inf; falsifying none. Normal = within one and a half times the pre-AI baseline's reading at the same age (the January 2021 baseline sat near 5 pp forty months in); fast = 10 pp or more, twice the pre-AI pace. Between is `emerging`.
- Timing: Lagging: the occupational mix moves only as workers change jobs over years, and the index is updated a few times a year.
